Alpha amylase is defined
Catalysis of the endohydrolysis of (1->4)-alpha-D-glucosidic linkages in polysaccharides containing three or more alpha-(1->4)-linked D-glucose units.

but pombe does not appear to have this activity:


"While classical α-amylases hydrolyze α-1,4-glucans, S. pombe cell lysates and their cultured media have no detectable α-amylase activity (29). And, like Ags1, the GH13 domains of these GH13 domain-containing proteins lack key catalytic residues typical of hydrolytic activity (28, 30). Thus, they are suggested to act as transglycosylases, enzymes that cleave and rejoin glucan chains, suggesting roles in α-glucan remodeling (31, 32). The shared features with Ags1 raise the possibility that these α-amylase-like proteins act in concert with or in parallel to Ags1 to assemble or extend α-glucan chains in the cell wall."

All references can be found within
PMID:40668835
Title | α-glucan remodeling by GH13-domain enzymes shapes fungal cell wall architecture.

author: Antonialock
body: This paper https://journals.asm.org/doi/full/10.1128/ec.00354-06 says that "The enzymes, designated AgtA and AgtB, produced new α-(1,4)-glycosidic bonds and therefore belong to the group of the 4-α-glucanotransferases (EC 2.4.1.25)." (aah4=meu7)

author: Antonialock
body: can I use this to infer that at least the aah1-3 pombe (Sp) proteins are EC 2.4.1.25 by similarity? (I haven't read the papers in detail yet, but it looks like also EXP evidence for process for aah1 and aah3 in the paper Val referenced)

author: ValWood
body:
I think probably yes, Aliana and Kathy speculate here:

https://www.pombase.org/reference/PMID:40668835

 This suggests that Aah1 and Aah3 belong in a subclass of GH13 enzymes like the Aspergillus niger GPI- anchored GH13 enzymes that do not hydrolyze but rather exhibit 4-α-glucanotransferase (disproportionation) (30), moving glucan units between chains to adjust polymer length.

Was originally thought to function as an alpha-amylase, but this activity is not detectable in S.pombe cell lysates or culture media.
